subject: Discovery recap + competitive-eval scope (benchmarks & acceptance criteria)
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Lucy Chang <lucy@quantaanalytics.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap + competitive-eval scope (benchmarks & acceptance criteria)

Hi Lucy — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap so we’re aligned and to document next steps for the competitive evaluation you asked us to participate in.

Pain points you shared:
- Unreliable latency at scale for user-facing generation (p95 spikes).
- High per-token cost from current cloud-hosted endpoints when batching is suboptimal.
- Observability gaps (token-level cost, per-route latency) and lack of deterministic rollbacks when quality regresses.

Current stack you described:
- Front-end: customer web app (Node) calling an inference microservice.
- Inference: currently mixing vLLM for internal experiments and a managed cloud endpoint for production (auto-scaling enabled).
- Storage: Redis for short-term KV cache, S3 for longer-term artifacts.

Success criteria for a win in the bake-off (as we captured):
- Latency: p95 generation latency at or below 350ms for 512-token sequences under the target throughput.
- Throughput: sustain 120 concurrent requests (avg request size ~350 tokens) without >10% tail latency degradation.
- Cost: per-1k-token cost reduction >= 35% vs their current managed cloud endpoint baseline.
- Quality: semantic parity with vLLM baseline on the 20 eval prompts you provided (we’ll run Rouge/embedding-similarity checks + human spot-checks).
- Operational: token-level cost and per-route traces visible in the console; ability to pin model versions and automatic fallback.

Requested benchmark artifacts from Quanta for the running test:
- Representative prompt set (20–50 prompts) — you mentioned you’ll attach a sample.
- Baseline metrics from the cloud endpoint (p50/p95/p99, error rates, cost per 1k tokens).
- Typical sequence length distribution and concurrent QPS target.

Proposed Redwood deliverables for the eval:
- Eval template (attached) with test harness, scripts to replay your prompt set, and how we will measure latency/throughput/cost.
- A short SOW draft for the bake-off scope and timeline.
- Two model configurations to test: (1) Quantized high-throughput variant (Redwood-qt-1) and (2) High-quality variant (Redwood-hq-1). Both will be compared to your vLLM and managed cloud endpoint results.

Next steps (pending your confirmation):
1) You share the sample prompts + baseline metrics and a target window for the test (you suggested Wed/Thu next week).
2) We provision a dedicated sandpit with the eval harness and run both configurations against your set.
3) We deliver a results deck with acceptance criteria mapping and recommendations.

Attachments: Redwood-eval-template.xlsx (eval harness & metrics), R-Requirements-Checklist.pdf

If that summary looks right I’ll schedule the sandbox run and loop in infra to reserve capacity.

Thanks — D

--
Dylan Brooks
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
D: +1 (415) 555-0198
From: Lucy Chang <lucy@quantaanalytics.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap + competitive-eval scope (benchmarks & acceptance criteria)

Dylan — this is great and captures everything we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Acceptance / quality details: for the semantic parity checks we typically run embedding-similarity + two human raters on a 20-prompt subset. If you can include the exact thresholds you plan to use (e.g., cosine > 0.88) that will help our reviewers.
2) Runtime env: our production service uses a mixture of g4dn-style instances for the managed endpoint and our vLLM experiments are on a local DGX cluster. Please account for both as baselines.
3) Data privacy: we need confirmation that logs and prompts used in the sandbox will be deleted after 30 days and that no prompts will be used to further train models.

We can share the prompt set and baseline metrics by EOD Tue. Wed/Thu next week works — prefer Thu morning PST for the sandbox run if possible.

I’ll also attach the baseline metrics (p50/p95/p99 + cost) in a follow-up. We’re excited to see the results vs vLLM/TGI and our managed endpoint.

—Lucy
Director of AI Platform
Quanta Analytics
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Discovery recap + competitive-eval scope (internal action items)

Grace / Rishi — forwarding Lucy's note. Quick internal split of responsibilities if we proceed: 
- Grace: own sandbox provisioning (GPU type, node count) and confirm cost estimate. Need a 4-GPU sandpit (A10G or equivalent) and at least 120 concurrent simulated clients for the replay.
- Rishi: finalize the eval harness scripts in Redwood-eval-template.xlsx; add the embedding-similarity thresholds (cosine >= 0.88) and human-rater workflow. Also confirm data-retention/privacy controls to reassure Quanta (auto-delete after 30 days, no training usage).

I’ll draft the short SOW and reach back to Lucy with proposed Thu morning PST slot and attach the SOW + eval template.

Thanks — D
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Lucy Chang <lucy@quantaanalytics.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Confirmed: Thu morning PST sandbox + attached eval artifacts

Lucy — thanks for the quick turnaround. Per your note we’ve attached the eval template and a short SOW draft (SOW-draft.docx). Highlights and explicit acceptance criteria we’ll measure during the run: 

Benchmarks we will record:
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 for 50/250/512 token sequences. Target: p95 <= 350ms for 512 sequences.
- Throughput: Sustained QPS at target concurrency with error rate <= 1%.
- Cost: measured per 1k tokens for each configuration.
- Quality: embedding cosine similarity (>= 0.88) + human rating pass rate >= 90% on the 20-prompt subset.

Comparators: vLLM (your local baseline), TGI (open-source endpoint you requested), and your managed cloud endpoint. We’ll run each comparator under the same prompt set and replay conditions.

Privacy & retention: sandpit logs and prompts will be stored only in the project's isolated bucket and will be deleted automatically after 30 days; we won’t use the data for model training. I’ve added a short appendix in the SOW for the retention clause.

Proposed time: Thu 14 May 2026, 09:30 AM PST. Please confirm. Attached: Redwood-eval-template.xlsx, R-Requirements-Checklist.pdf, SOW-draft.docx

Best — D
From: Lucy Chang <lucy@quantaanalytics.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Confirmed: Thu morning PST sandbox + attached eval artifacts

Dylan — confirmed for Thu 14 May 2026, 09:30 AM PST. Appreciate the retention language in the SOW. I attached the prompt set and baseline metrics in my earlier message (let me know if you didn’t receive them; I’ll resend). Also attaching a preliminary PO for budget planning.

Looking forward to the run — Lucy
